title: Mind over matter

questions.hint: The cloth in Jeremiah's rescue protected the places where narrow ropes pressed against his body.
questions.prompt: A wider backpack strap spreads the same load over more of your shoulder. Which physical quantity does this reduce?
questions.reference: Jeremiah 38:12–13 · Original clue (not a Bible quotation)
questions.explanation: Cloth protected Jeremiah where the rescue ropes contacted his body. Padding can distribute the supporting force over a larger effective area, connecting the rescue to reduced pressure under a wider strap.

questions.hint: Isaac's hands suggested one brother, but his ears suggested the other.
questions.prompt: A flute and a violin play the same note at the same loudness. Which sound property chiefly lets you tell them apart?
questions.reference: Genesis 27:22 · Original clue (not a Bible quotation)
questions.explanation: Isaac distinguishes a familiar voice despite conflicting touch evidence. Recognizable vocal quality provides a route to timbre, which also helps distinguish instruments playing the same note.

questions.hint: The fleece behind Job's act of kindness has many tiny spaces between its fibers.
questions.prompt: What is the main way the fluffy structure of a wool sweater helps keep you warm?
answers: It traps air that slows heat transfer
It conducts body heat toward the skin
It reflects nearly all outgoing heat
It blocks heat loss by absorbing moisture
questions.reference: Job 31:20 · Original clue (not a Bible quotation)
questions.explanation: Job associates sheep's fleece with warmth. The clue adds wool's fibrous structure, inviting the inference that trapped air provides insulation; the passage itself does not explain heat transfer.

description: Three questions. Give it some thought.
